By utilizing a <cite id="11">direct service model</cite>, they bypass many of the administrative layers that typically inflate costs in international aid. rich_narrative.summary: The Sudanese American Physicians Association (SAPA) is a medical relief organization that provides critical healthcare and humanitarian aid to vulnerable populations in Sudan and Chad. Founded in 2019, the organization has demonstrated <cite id="1">early-stage growth</cite>, rapidly scaling its operations to address the escalating humanitarian crisis in the region. In FY2024, SAPA managed <cite id="2">$7,254,154 in total revenue</cite> to support its healthcare and emergency services. The organization maintains a <cite id="3">90/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting a strong commitment to financial health and accountability. SAPA operates through a direct service model, delivering aid across five core program areas: <cite id="4">Healthcare and Emergency Services, Hunger Relief, WASH, Empowering Physicians, and Project NOOR</cite>. This direct approach allows the charity to maintain an exceptionally low <cite id="5">cost of approximately $6.96 per beneficiary</cite>, which is considered highly efficient for the global health sector. Furthermore, the organization is <cite id="6">verified as zakat-eligible</cite>, specifically serving the asnaf categories of the poor (fuqara) and needy (masakin). By leveraging a network of Sudanese-American medical professionals, SAPA provides specialized expertise that is often missing in general humanitarian responses, ensuring that medical interventions are both culturally appropriate and technically sound.
